record.title: Conjecture on the support of topological limiting measures
record.statement: Let ${\bf M}$ be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold with a totally geodesic surface. Let $h_0=h_0({\bf M})$ be the genus of a totally geodesic surface of smallest genus in ${\bf M}$, and let ${\mathcal H}_{h_0}$ denote the corresponding subset of the space of surfaces. **Support conjecture.** Every topological limiting measure is supported on ${\mathcal H}_{h_0}$. The preceding theorem says that every topological limiting measure is totally scarring, while this conjecture predicts the more precise genus of the totally geodesic surfaces carrying its support. Its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: Jeremy Kahn, Vladimir Markovic and Ilia Smilga, “Geometrically and topologically random surfaces in a closed hyperbolic three manifold”, arXiv:2309.02847 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02847

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Gyárfás–Lehel covering conjecture for cross-intersecting partite hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be non-empty cross-intersecting hypergraphs: every edge of $A$ meets every edge of $B$. Suppose both are $r$-partite and share the same $r$-partition. A **cover** of $A\cup B$ is a set of vertices meeting every edge, and $\tau(A\cup B)$ denotes its minimum size.

**Gyárfás–Lehel conjecture.** Then

$$
\tau(A\cup B)\leqslant 2r-2.
$$

The bound improves the elementary bound obtained from the union of one edge of each hypergraph. The source presents this as open and notes that the bound is tight if true.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Joseph Briggs, He Guo and Shira Zerbib, “Looms”, arXiv:2309.03735 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03735

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “The conjecture is open for $r\ge 4$.”

record.title: Fractional covering conjecture for looms
record.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be hypergraphs forming an $(r,s)$-loom, and write $\mathbb{L}=(A,B)$. Define the fractional covering number of the loom by

$$
\tau^*(\mathbb{L})=\tau^*(A\cup B).
$$

Here $\tau^*$ is the minimum total weight of a nonnegative fractional vertex cover.

**Loom fractional covering conjecture.** If $\mathbb{L}=(A,B)$ is an $(r,s)$-loom, then

$$
\tau^*(\mathbb{L})=\max(r,s).
$$

The source has the upper bound $\tau^*(\mathbb{L})\leqslant\max(r,s)$ and proposes equality; it also notes that this conjecture would imply the Gyárfás–Lehel conjecture in the equal-uniformity setting. It remains open.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Joseph Briggs, He Guo and Shira Zerbib, “Looms”, arXiv:2309.03735 (2024).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “The conjecture is open for $r\ge 4$.”

record.title: Even-order off-diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrix generating-function symmetry conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X^{\mathrm O}_{2n}(r,t)$ be the even-order OSASM generating function, and let $\bar t$ denote the parameter appearing in the source's generating-function notation. For an OSASM $A$, let $R(A)$ and $T(A)$ denote the statistics used to define this generating function. **Even-order OSASM symmetry conjecture.** The generating function satisfies

$$
X^{\mathrm O}_{2n}(r,t)=t^{2n+2}X^{\mathrm O}_{2n}(r,\bar t).
$$

Equivalently, for every $rho$ and $tau$,

$$
|\{A\in\mathrm{OSASM}(2n):R(A)=\rho,\ T(A)=\tau\}|
=
|\{A\in\mathrm{OSASM}(2n):R(A)=\rho,\ T(A)=2n+2-\tau\}|.
$$

The conjecture also asserts the coefficient identity

$$
[t^3]X^{\mathrm O}_{2n}(r,t)=[t^{2n-1}]X^{\mathrm O}_{2n}(r,t)=r\bigl((n-2)r^2+1\bigr)X^{\mathrm O}_{2n-2}(r,1).
$$

These claims describe a proposed symmetry of the refined enumeration of even-order OSASMs; the paper presents them as conjectural and supplies no proof.
record.source_name: Roger E. Behrend, Ilse Fischer and Christoph Koutschan, “Diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices”, arXiv:2309.08446 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08446

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2023). “This conjecture was first proved by Zeilberger , and further proofs involving other methods were subsequently obtained by Kuperberg , Fischer , and Fischer and Konvalinka .”

record.title: The $=5$ case of Vizing's conjecture for triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $5$-regular triangle-free graph.

**The $=5$ case of Vizing's conjecture.** Every $5$-regular triangle-free graph has chromatic number at most $4$.

This is identified in the source as the current smallest open case of the broader triangle-free graph coloring conjecture. The source notes that the corresponding bound is known for maximum degree at most $4$, but this $5$-regular case was presented as open.
record.source_name: Ross J. Kang and Matthieu Rosenfeld, “On Vizing's problem for triangle-free graphs”, arXiv:2309.10876 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10876

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2023). “This aligns with one of the few remaining cases of an old and largely refuted conjecture of Gr\"unbaum ; he actually conjectured the negation of this.”

record.title: Magnant–Martin path-cover conjecture for regular digraphs and oriented graphs
record.statement:
For a digraph $G$, let $\pi(G)$ denote the minimum number of vertex-disjoint directed paths needed to cover $V(G)$. A **$d$-regular digraph** has indegree and outdegree $d$ at every vertex; an oriented graph is a digraph with at most one directed edge between each pair of vertices.

**Magnant–Martin's strengthened conjecture.** If $G$ is a $d$-regular digraph on $n$ vertices, then

$$
\pi(G)\leq \frac{n}{d+1}.
$$

Moreover, if $G$ is oriented, then

$$
\pi(G)\leq \frac{n}{2d+1}.
$$

The paper proves these bounds in the dense setting, namely for sufficiently large $n$ when $d\geq\alpha n$ for fixed $f70b>0$. The conjecture is proposed as a stronger directed and oriented analogue of the regular-graph path-cover conjecture.
record.source_name: Allan Lo, Viresh Patel and Mehmet Akif Yıldız, “Cycle Partitions in Dense Regular Digraphs and Oriented Graphs”, arXiv:2309.11677 (2025).
record.references:

The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2212.12793](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12793), [arXiv:1911.08397](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.08397), [arXiv:1809.04394](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.04394), [arXiv:1807.10613](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.10613), [arXiv:1706.06945](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06945).

record.title: Magnant–Wang–Yuan path-cover conjecture for graphs with prescribed degree bounds
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\pi(G)$ denote the minimum number of vertex-disjoint paths needed to cover $V(G)$. Let $n=|V(G)|$, and write $\Delta(G)=\Delta$ and $\delta(G)=\delta$ for the maximum and minimum degrees.

**Magnant–Wang–Yuan's conjecture.** The path-cover number satisfies

$$
\pi(G)\leq \max\left\{\frac{n}{\delta+1},\frac{(\Delta-\delta)n}{\Delta+\delta}\right\}.
$$

The bound is tight for disjoint unions of $K_{\delta+1}$ and of $K_{\delta,\Delta}$. The conjecture is known when $\delta\leq 2$ and when $\Delta\geq 2\delta$, but remains open in general according to the source.

record.title: Bernshteyn–Lee's lower-bound conjecture for weak degeneracy of regular graphs
record.statement:
A graph $G$ is **weakly $d$-degenerate** if it is weakly $f$-degenerate for the constant function with value $d$, and its weak degeneracy $\operatorname{wd}(G)$ is the minimum such integer $d$. **Bernshteyn–Lee's conjecture.** Every $d$-regular graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{wd}(G)\geqslant d-O(\sqrt{d}).
$$

The conjecture would improve the general lower bound $\operatorname{wd}(G)\geqslant d-\sqrt{2n}$ for a $d$-regular graph with $n\geqslant2$ vertices, showing that weak degeneracy is close to the degree independently of the graph's order. The trivial upper bound is $d$, attained by complete graphs.

record.title: The perfect diameter-two graph conjecture for 2-bootstrap percolation
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the collection of all connected graphs of order at least $3$ with at most two blocks. A graph is **2-bootstrap good** if it contains at least one pair of vertices that percolate under the $r=2$ bootstrap percolation process. A graph is perfect if every induced subgraph has a vertex whose neighborhood is a clique, and its diameter is the maximum graph distance between two vertices. **The perfect diameter-two graph conjecture.** If a graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is perfect and its diameter is no more than $2$, then the graph is 2-bootstrap good. This would give a sufficient structural condition for 2-bootstrap goodness within the class $\mathcal{G}$; the supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Hudson LaFayette, Rayan Ibrahim and Kevin McCall, “Bootstrap Percolation, Connectivity, and Graph Distance”, arXiv:2309.13138 (2023).

record.title: The H¹ strong cosmic censorship conjecture for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged-Klein-Gordon system
record.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a regular, compact spacelike hypersurface without boundary. Prescribe generic initial data in the spherically symmetric class for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged-Klein-Gordon system with $\Lambda>0$, and let its future maximal globally hyperbolic development be the largest Lorentzian development determined by these data. **$H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ strong cosmic censorship conjecture.** This development cannot be locally extended as a Lorentzian manifold endowed with a continuous metric and Christoffel symbols in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. This is a stronger regularity formulation than mere continuous inextendibility and is motivated by the regularity needed to interpret extensions as weak solutions of the Einstein equations. The source does not establish the conjecture as a theorem.

record.title: Chowla subspace matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K\subset L$ be a field extension, and let $A$ and $B$ be two $n$-dimensional $K$-subspaces of $L$. A $K$-subspace $B$ is called a **Chowla subspace** if every nonzero $b\in B$ satisfies

$$
[K(b):K]\geq \dim_K B+1.
$$

**Chowla matching conjecture.** If $B$ is a Chowla subspace, then $A$ is matched to $B$.

This is proposed as a linear counterpart to the corresponding matching theorem for Chowla subsets in abelian groups. The source notes that primitive subspaces in finite separable extensions are Chowla subspaces and gives a lower bound for the maximum possible dimension, but the asserted matching statement remains unresolved.

record.title: Two-sided Curto–Herrero conjecture for tuples of matrices
record.statement:
Let $M_n^m$ be the space of $m$-tuples of $n\times n$ matrices over a field, and let ${\rm GL}_n$ act by simultaneous conjugation. For ${\underline{A}}=(A_1,\ldots,A_m)$, write $f({\underline{A}})$ for the evaluation of a noncommutative polynomial $f$ in the tuple.

**Two-sided Curto–Herrero conjecture.** For every ${\underline{A}},{\underline{B}}\in M_n^m$, the ${\rm GL}_n$-orbits of ${\underline{A}}$ and ${\underline{B}}$ coincide if and only if

$$
\operatorname{rank} f({\underline{A}})=\operatorname{rank} f({\underline{B}})
$$

for every noncommutative polynomial $f$ in $m$ variables, possibly with a free term.

The conjecture is refuted in general for $n\geq3$ and $m\geq2$ by a counterexample of Hadwin and Larson. It does hold for $m=1$, by the rational canonical form; related rank criteria using matrices of noncommutative polynomials are captured by the solved two-sided Hadwin–Larson conjecture.
record.source_name: Jennyfer Juliana Calderón Moreno and Artem Lopatin, “Pairs of matrices with simple spectrum”, arXiv:2310.00476 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.00476

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Hadwin and Larson in 2003 gave a counterexample (see Example 5 of ) to the weaker two-sided Curto--Herrero conjecture:”

record.title: Conjecture on extremal Hamiltonian paths in the unit cube
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite point set in the unit cube $[0,1]^k$. For a graph $G$ on vertex set $X$, define its scaled cost by

$$
s_k(G)=\left(\sum_{e\in G}|e|^k\right)^{1/k}.
$$

Let $s_k^{\texttt{HP}}(X)$ be the minimum scaled cost over Hamiltonian paths on $X$, and set

$$
s_k^{\texttt{HP}}=\sup_{n\geq 2}\sup_{X\subseteq[0,1]^k,\,|X|=n}s_k^{\texttt{HP}}(X).
$$

**Hamiltonian-path conjecture.** The equalities

$$
s_k^{\texttt{HP}}=\begin{cases}\sqrt{3},&k=2,\\left(2^{k-1}-1\right)^{1/k}\sqrt{2},&k=3,4,5,6,\\sqrt{k},&k\geq 7\end{cases}
$$

hold.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen and Adrian Dumitrescu, “On a Traveling Salesman Problem for Points in the Unit Cube”, arXiv:2310.02839 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.02839

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Conjecture P(k,r) for intersections of longest paths
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and $r\leq k$. A graph is **$k$-connected** if, for any two distinct vertices, it has $k$ internally disjoint paths between them. A **longest path** is a path of maximum length. **Conjecture P$(k,r)$.** In any $k$-connected graph, every pair of longest paths intersect in at least $r$ vertices.

This family includes the path-intersection claims discussed earlier, with $r=k$ giving Hippchen's conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution status for the family.
record.source_name: Juan Gutiérrez and Christian Valqui, “On two conjectures about the intersection of longest paths and cycles”, arXiv:2310.03849 (2023).

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2023). “For Hippchen's conjecture, the case $k=3$ was proved by Hippchen himself .”

record.title: The ordered matching conjecture
record.statement: An **ordered graph** is a graph together with a total vertex ordering. **The ordered matching conjecture.** Let $(M,\prec)$ be an ordered graph with maximum degree $1$. Then the class of $(M,\prec)$-free ordered graphs is $\chi$-bounded. The paper explains that this would imply dichromatic binding for tournaments admitting a backedge graph of maximum degree $1$; the conjecture is attributed to Briański, Davies and Walczak.

record.title: Fujita–Lo–Zhang conjecture on properly colored cycles in edge-colored complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{m,n}$ be a complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $m$ and $n$, equipped with an edge-coloring, and let $\delta^c(K_{m,n})$ be its minimum color degree, where the color degree of a vertex is the number of distinct colors on its incident edges. A **properly colored cycle** is a cycle whose adjacent edges have distinct colors. **Fujita–Lo–Zhang conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^c(K_{m,n})\geq \frac{m+n}{4}+1,
$$

then every vertex of $K_{m,n}$ lies on a properly colored cycle of every even length $l$ satisfying

$$
4\leq l\leq \min\{2m,2n\}.
$$

This conjecture predicts vertex-even-pancyclicity under a minimum color-degree condition in edge-colored complete bipartite graphs; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Shanshan Guo, Fei Huang, Jinjiang Yuan, C. T. Ng and T. C. E. Cheng, “Properly colored even cycles in edge-colored complete balanced bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2310.04962 (2023).

record.title: Gao–Han–Peng–Sun conjecture for Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constants
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $\beta=\exp(G)$ denote its exponent, and let $k\in\mathbb N$. The invariant $\mathsf{s}_{k\beta}(G)$ is the smallest length guaranteeing a zero-sum subsequence of length $k\beta$, while $\mathsf D(G)$ is the Davenport constant. **Gao–Han–Peng–Sun conjecture.** If $k\beta\ge \mathsf D(G)$, then

$$
\mathsf{s}_{k\beta}(G)=k\beta+\mathsf D(G)-1.
$$

The conjecture extends Gao’s result from the condition $k\exp(G)\ge |G|$ to the weaker condition $k\exp(G)\ge\mathsf D(G)$. The source states that it remains open in specific rank-three $2$- and $3$-group cases.
record.source_name: Shiwen Zhang, “On some zero-sum invariants for abelian groups of rank three”, arXiv:2310.05458 (2023).

record.title: Oliveira et al.'s extremal conjecture for the signless Laplacian spectrum
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple graph on $n$ vertices, let $S_2(G)$ denote the sum of its two largest signless Laplacian eigenvalues, and define

$$
f(G)=e(G)+3-S_2(G).
$$

Let $K^+_{1,n-1}$ denote the star graph with an additional edge. **Oliveira et al.'s conjecture.** For any graph $G$ on $n\geq 9$ vertices,

$$
f(G)\geq f(K^+_{1,n-1}).
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G\cong K^+_{1,n-1}$. The paper states that this conjecture is proved in the present work, so it is solved.
record.source_name: Zi-Ming Zhou, Chang-Xiang He and Hai-Ying Shan, “On the sum of the first two largest signless Laplacian eigenvalues of a graph”, arXiv:2310.08880 (2024).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2023). “Therefore, for general graphs Conjecture is still open when $k=2$.”

record.title: Ashraf et al.'s signless Laplacian eigenvalue-sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $S_k(G)$ denote the sum of the first $k$ largest signless Laplacian eigenvalues of $G$. **Ashraf et al.'s conjecture.** For any graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and any $k\in\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$,

$$
S_k(G)\leq e(G)+\binom{k+1}{2}.
$$

The conjecture is known for several classes, including regular graphs and connected triangle-free graphs when $k=2$, but remains open for general graphs when $k=2$.

record.title: The packed-set conjecture for EvenQuads
record.statement: Let an EvenQuads deck be a vector space of binary cards, and let a **complete set** of $2^k$ cards mean a $k$-dimensional subspace (or its affine translate). For a set of $ell$ cards, write $Q(\ell)$ for its number of quads, and call a set **packed** if it realizes the maximum possible number of quads among sets of the same size. Let $p=2^{\lceil\log_2 \ell\rceil}$. **Packed-set conjecture.** If a set of $ell$ cards is not contained in a complete set of $p$ cards, then it has at most as many quads as an $(\ell-1)$-packed set. This conjecture is intended to control the extremal structure of sets of cards in the EvenQuads deck and underlies the proposed formula for the maximum number of quads. The supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Universal inverse-degree upper bound for critical percolation
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an infinite, connected, transitive, simple graph of vertex degree $d$ that is not one-dimensional, and let $p_c(G)$ be its Bernoulli bond percolation critical probability. **Universal inverse-degree conjecture.** There exists a universal constant $C$ such that

$$
p_c(G)\leq\frac{C}{d}.
$$

This conjecture would strengthen known uniform gaps below $1$ for Cayley graphs and would imply, together with locality, that $p_c$ attains a global maximum on the space of non-one-dimensional transitive graphs. The source leaves the conjecture open.

record.title: The vanishing minimal deviation angle conjecture for networks
record.statement: Let $N$ be the dimension of the network, and let the minimal deviation angle be the minimum deviation angle arising from the network's admissible vectors as defined in the surrounding discussion. **Vanishing minimal deviation angle conjecture.** The minimal deviation angle is equal to zero for any $N$. The claim is proved in the source for $N=2$, while the general case is presented as very likely but is not established there.

record.title: The minimum codegree threshold for resolvable Steiner triple systems
record.statement: Let $n$ be sufficiently large with $n\equiv 3\pmod{6}$, and let $H$ be a hypergraph on $n$ vertices. A **resolvable Steiner triple system** is a Steiner triple system whose triples can be partitioned into perfect matchings. **The resolvable Steiner triple system conjecture.** There are constants $n_0$ and $C$ such that, whenever $n\ge n_0$ and $H$ has minimum codegree at least $(3/4)n+C$, the hypergraph $H$ contains a resolvable Steiner triple system. Resolvable Steiner triple systems exist on $n$ vertices exactly when $n\equiv3\pmod 6$, but the asserted minimum-codegree threshold remains open.

record.title: Odd-sunflower exponential bound conjecture
record.statement: A **$k$-uniform family** is a family of sets in which every set has size $k$. An **odd-sunflower** is a family of at least two sets such that every element of the underlying set belongs to an odd number of the sets or to none of them. **Odd-sunflower exponential bound conjecture.** The maximum size of any odd-sunflower-free $k$-uniform family is at most $c^k$ for a suitable constant $c>0$. This is posed as a weakening of the Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture and is left open in the paper.
record.source_name: Peter Frankl, János Pach and Dömötör Pálvölgyi, “Odd-Sunflowers”, arXiv:2310.16701 (2024).

record.title: Sunflower-free base-size exponential bound conjecture
record.statement: For a sunflower-free $k$-uniform family, its **base elements** are the elements contained in at least one set of the family. **Sunflower-free base-size exponential bound conjecture.** The maximum number of base elements in a sunflower-free $k$-uniform family is at most $c^k$ for a suitable constant $c>0$. This conjecture was posed in the first version of the paper and is presented as a separate weakening related to the Erdős–Rado sunflower problem; the paper does not report a resolution.

record.title: Maximal hypertriangulations are maximum
record.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be finite and generic. A level-$k$ hypertriangulation is **maximal** if no other hypertriangulation of the same level subdivides it, and it is **maximum** if no other hypertriangulation of the same level has more triangles.

**Maximality conjecture.** Any two maximal level-$k$ hypertriangulations of $A$ have the same, and therefore maximum, number of triangles. Equivalently, every maximal level-$k$ hypertriangulation is maximum.

This conjecture seeks to extend the known relationship between completeness and maximality beyond level $2$; its validity for general levels is open.
record.source_name: Herbert Edelsbrunner, Alexey Garber and Morteza Saghafian, “Order-2 Delaunay Triangulations Optimize Angles”, arXiv:2310.18238 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18238

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Minimum-semidegree conjecture for balanced antidirected trees
record.statement: Let $D$ be an oriented graph on $n$ vertices, let $\delta^0(D)$ denote its minimum semidegree, and let a balanced antidirected tree have equally many sources and sinks. **The balanced-tree conjecture.** Every oriented $n$-vertex graph $D$ with $\delta^0(D)>k/2$ contains every balanced antidirected $k$-edge tree whose total maximum degree is at most $o(n)$. The conjecture concerns the threshold below the trivial greedy bound and remains open.
record.source_name: Maya Stein, “Oriented trees and paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2310.18719 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: The conjectural double Fourier–Mellin transform formula over the complex numbers
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an integer, let $\beta,\gamma,\nu\in\mathbb{C}$, and let $u,\varw\in\mathbb{C}$ satisfy

$$
\operatorname{Re}(1/(u\varw))<1.
$$

For the Bessel function $\boldsymbol{B}_{\nu,p}$ and the associated function $\boldsymbol{H}_{\nu,p}^{\beta-\gamma}$, **the double Fourier–Mellin transform conjecture.** The integral formula

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\int\!\!\int\!\!\int\!\!\int \boldsymbol{B}_{\nu,p}(\sqrt{\varv z})e\bigl(-2\operatorname{Re}(uz+\varw\varv)\bigr)\frac{i\,dz\wedge d\widebar{z}}{|z|^{2-2\beta}}\frac{i\,d\varv\wedge d\widebar{\varv}}{|\varv|^{2-2\gamma}} \\
&\qquad=\frac{2}{(2\pi)^{2\beta+2\gamma}|u|^{2\beta}|\varw|^{2\gamma}}\,{}^{\beta+\gamma}\!\boldsymbol{H}_{\nu,p}^{\beta-\gamma}\!\left(\frac{1}{u\varw}\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

is valid whenever

$$
|\operatorname{Re}(\nu)|<\operatorname{Re}(2\beta)<\frac{3}{2},\qquad |\operatorname{Re}(\nu)|<\operatorname{Re}(2\gamma)<\min\bigl\{1+\operatorname{Re}(2\beta),3-\operatorname{Re}(2\beta)\bigr\}.
$$

This conjecture extends the preceding complex double Fourier–Mellin identity from even $p$ to arbitrary $p$ and general Mellin exponents. Its validity is motivated by the corresponding real-variable formulas, but the supplied text gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Zhi Qi, “On the Hankel Transform of Bessel Functions on Complex Numbers and Explicit Spectral Formulae over the Gaussian Field”, arXiv:2310.19480 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19480

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: The possibility of non-square congruence subgroups for linear level polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be such that $\alpha\neq 0$, and consider the congruence subgroups $\Gamma_1(\alpha T+\beta)$ and $\Gamma_0(\alpha T+\beta)$. A congruence subgroup is called **non-square** when it does not satisfy the paper's notion of being square.

**Non-square congruence subgroup conjecture.** Both $\Gamma_1(\alpha T+\beta)$ and $\Gamma_0(\alpha T+\beta)$ may be non-square congruence subgroups for any choice of $\alpha\neq 0$ and $\beta$.

The claim concerns the stabilizers of elliptic points and is used to determine the relevant geometric invariants of the associated Drinfeld modular curves. The supplied context does not state whether this possibility has been established or remains open.
record.source_name: Jesse Franklin, “The Geometry of Drinfeld Modular Forms”, arXiv:2310.19623 (2024).

record.title: Saks's extremal gap conjecture for heights of incomparable elements
record.statement:
For a poset $P$, let $h(P,x)$ denote the average height of $x$, and let $\eta(P)$ be the smallest absolute difference $|h(P,x)-h(P,y)|$ over incomparable elements $x,y$. Set

$$
\vartheta=\frac14\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\left(1-\frac1{2^k}\right)^{-1}.
$$
 **Saks’s gap conjecture.** Every poset $P$ that is not a chain satisfies

$$
\eta(P)\leq\vartheta.
$$
 The source gives constructions approaching $\vartheta$ and reports the conjecture as open.
record.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Linear extensions of finite posets”, arXiv:2311.02743 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02743

record.title: List chromatic number conjecture for multipartite uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $k\geqslant 2$, let $\Delta$ be sufficiently large, and let $H$ be a $k$-partite $k$-graph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$. Write $\chi_\ell(H)$ for the list chromatic number of $H$. **List chromatic number conjecture for $k$-partite $k$-graphs.** There is a constant $c=c(k)>0$ such that

$$
\chi_\ell(H)\leqslant c\log\Delta.
$$

This extends the Alon–Krivelevich conjecture from bipartite graphs to $k$-partite $k$-graphs and is supported by results for random and complete multipartite hypergraphs. The case $k=2$ matches the cited bipartite conjecture; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Abhishek Dhawan, “List colorings of k-partite k-graphs”, arXiv:2311.03111 (2025).
record.references:

record.title: Edmonds–Giles weighted dijoin packing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph with arc weights $w
i\{0,1\}^A$. The **weight of a dicut** is the sum of the weights of its arcs, and the **minimum dicut weight** is the smallest such weight. The digraph **packs** $k$ dijoins if it has $k$ dijoins such that no arc $e$ belongs to more than $w(e)$ of them.

**Edmonds–Giles conjecture.** If the minimum weight of a dicut is $\tau$, then $D$ can pack $\tau$ dijoins.

The conjecture was disproved by Schrijver, so the corresponding weighted packing assertion is false; its unweighted version is Woodall's still-open conjecture.
record.source_name: Gérard Cornuéjols, Siyue Liu and R. Ravi, “Approximately Packing Dijoins via Nowhere-Zero Flows”, arXiv:2311.04337 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.04337

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2023); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Mixed-graph pseudo-dicut orientation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M=(V,E\cup A)$ be a mixed graph, where $A$ is the set of directed arcs and $E$ the set of undirected edges. For $U\subset V$, a **pseudo dicut** is the edge set $\delta_E(U)$ such that no directed arc enters $U$. An **orientation** $E^+$ of $E$ replaces every undirected edge by a directed edge. For an oriented cut, write $\delta_{E^+}^+(U)$ and $\delta_{E^+}^-(U)$ for its outgoing and incoming edges.

**Mixed-graph orientation conjecture.** There is a constant $k>2$ such that for every mixed graph $M=(V,E\cup A)$, there is an orientation $E^+$ such that

$$
|\delta_{E^+}^+(U)|,|\delta_{E^+}^-(U)|\geq \left\lfloor\frac{1}{k}|\delta_E(U)|\right\rfloor
$$

for every pseudo dicut $\delta_E(U)$.

This is proposed as an analogue of nowhere-zero flow methods for mixed graphs. The source notes that the counterexample to Edmonds–Giles implies $k>2$, and gives no resolution.

record.title: Schleimer's distance formula conjecture for multiarc and curve graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a compact, connected, orientable surface, and let $\mathcal A$ be a multiarc and curve graph on $\Sigma$. For a witness $W$, let $\pi_W:\mathcal A\to 2^{\mathcal C W}\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ be subsurface projection and define

$$
d_W(a,b)=\operatorname{diam}_{\mathcal C W}(\pi_W(a)\cup\pi_W(b)).
$$

Let $\mathscr X$ denote the collection of witnesses of $\mathcal A$, let $[x]_C$ denote the thresholded quantity used in the distance formula, and write $d_{\mathcal A}(a,b)\stackrel{K,E}{=}r$ when the two quantities are equivalent up to multiplicative constant $K$ and additive constant $E$. Assume that $(a,b)\in E(\mathcal A)$ if and only if $i(a,b)\leq M$ for some $M\geq0$. **Schleimer's distance formula conjecture.** There exists $C'=C'(\mathcal A)$ such that for every $C>C'$, there are constants $K,E\geq0$ satisfying

$$
d_{\mathcal A}(a,b)\stackrel{K,E}{=}\sum_{W\in\mathscr X}[d_W(a,b)]_C.
$$

This is a proposed Masur--Minsky-style distance formula for multiarc and curve graphs. The source does not specify whether it has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Michael C. Kopreski, “Multiarc and curve graphs are hierarchically hyperbolic”, arXiv:2311.04356 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: The chromatic-number conjecture for irredundance compelling colorings
record.statement:
An **irredundance compelling coloring** ($IRC$-coloring) of a graph $G$ is a proper vertex coloring in which every color class is a minimal dominating set of $G$; a graph is $IRC$-colorable if it admits such a coloring, and $\chi(G)$ denotes its chromatic number.

**Chromatic-number conjecture.** Any $IRC$-colorable graph $G$ admits an $IRC$-coloring using $\chi(G)$ colors.

The conjecture asserts that whenever an $IRC$-coloring exists, the minimum number of colors in such a coloring equals the ordinary chromatic number. The source gives no resolution or supporting theorem beyond examples, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: David Ashok Kalarkop and Pawaton Kaemawichanurat, “On irredundance coloring and irredundance compelling coloring of graphs”, arXiv:2311.06161 (2023).

record.title: Gabow's exchange-distance conjecture for disjoint matroid bases
record.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$, and let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be disjoint bases. The **exchange distance** of two basis sequences is the minimum number of symmetric exchanges needed to transform one sequence into the other. **Gabow's conjecture.** The exchange distance of $(X_1,X_2)$ and $(X_2,X_1)$ is $r$. This problem was formulated by Gabow and later stated as a conjecture by Wiedemann and by Cordovil and Moreira. It is known for several classes of matroids, but remains open in general.

record.title: Kac–Weisfeiler's maximal simple-module dimension conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a restricted Lie algebra, and let $M(\mathfrak{g})$ denote the maximal dimension of a simple $U(\mathfrak{g})$-module.

**Kac–Weisfeiler conjecture (KW1).**

$$
M(\mathfrak{g})=p^{\frac{1}{2}(\dim(\mathfrak{g})-\operatorname{ind}(\mathfrak{g}))}.
$$

This is a modular representation-theoretic conjecture concerning the largest dimension of a simple module over the restricted enveloping algebra. It remains open in general, although it is known for several classes of restricted Lie algebras, and the paper proves it for the truncated current Lie algebras under consideration in the stated reductive-group setting.
record.source_name: Matthew Chaffe and Lewis Topley, “Modular Representations of Truncated current Lie algebras”, arXiv:2311.08208 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.08208

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2023). “The conjecture KW1 is still open in general, but some results for certain classes of Lie algebras are known.”

record.title: Chudnovsky–Nevo conjecture on independent sets in flag spheres
record.statement:
Let $\alpha(n,d)$ denote the minimum size of the largest independent set among all flag triangulations of $d$-spheres on $n$ vertices.

**Chudnovsky–Nevo conjecture.**

$$
\alpha(n,d)=\left\lceil\frac{n+d-2}{2d}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture gives a sharp linear lower bound for independent sets in flag triangulations of spheres, motivated by the study of their $f$-vectors. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied source.

record.title: Psi-expansion conjecture for interval graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=([n],E)$ be an interval graph. For a composition $\alpha\vDash n$, let $\Psi_\alpha$ be the type 1 power sum quasisymmetric function, let $z_\alpha=z_{\lambda(\alpha)}$, and let $\mathcal{N}_{G,\alpha}$ be the set of permutations defined by requiring that each segment of composition shape $\alpha$ has neither a $G$-descent nor a nontrivial left-to-right $G$-maximum. Let $\omega$ be the involution on $\operatorname{QSym}$. **First conjecture.**

$$
\omega \chi_G[X;q]=\sum_{\alpha\vDash n}\frac{\Psi_\alpha}{z_{\alpha}}\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{N}_{G,\alpha}}q^{\widetilde{\mathsf{inv}}_G(\sigma)}.
$$

This extends the power-sum expansion known for Dyck graphs and proposes a quasisymmetric analogue for interval graphs.
record.source_name: Michele D'Adderio, Roberto Riccardi and Viola Siconolfi, “Chromatic functions, interval orders and increasing forests”, arXiv:2311.09685 (2023).

record.title: Blidia et al.'s conjecture on b-colorings of regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph, and let its girth be the length of a shortest cycle. A **b-coloring** of $G$ is a proper vertex coloring in which each color class contains a vertex adjacent to at least one vertex in every other color class.

**Blidia et al.'s conjecture.** Every $d$-regular graph of girth at least $5$, different than the Petersen graph, has a b-coloring with $d+1$ colors.

The conjecture concerns when the b-chromatic number of a regular graph reaches the maximum possible value $d+1$. The source presents it as the main conjecture for regular graphs; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Magda Dettlaff, Hanna Furmańczyk, Iztok Peterin, Riana Roux and Radosław Ziemann, “A new approach to b-coloring of regular graphs”, arXiv:2311.13283 (2023).
